name: Massachusetts State House
description: The Massachusetts State House sits atop Beacon Hill at the western edge of Boston Common. It is home to the State Senate, the House of Representatives, and the Governor's Office. Its dome was first gilded in 23 karat gold leaf in 1874.
significance_text: Designed by Charles Bulfinch in 1787 and built in 1795-98, it is described in its National Historic Landmark nomination as one of the supreme examples of Federal-period civic architecture in the United States and the masterpiece of Bulfinch's public buildings. It is one of the oldest state capitols in continuous use in the country.

admission.notes: Free docent-led walking tours run on weekdays between 10:00am and 3:30pm and last about 45 minutes. Tours meet in Doric Hall. Self-guided materials are available. Groups are advised to schedule in advance.
